messages:
alex: Alert from hosted-pool-monitor — admission headroom for hosted-usw2-gpu-pool dipped to 3% over the last 5m. Dashboard: https://dash.redwood.ai/d/hosted/usw2-pool?panel=admission-headroom. Queue depth rising, KV cache evictions spiking.
ops-bot: [AUTO] alert triggered: admission_headroom < 5% (5m). runbook: https://go/redwood/runbooks/gpu-admission. payload: {pool: hosted-usw2, headroom: 3.1, qdepth: 420, kv_evictions_s: 245}.
jordan: seeing a big tail of short requests (~<40 tokens) driving queue, mostly from sandbox-canary route.
tanya: FYI I bumped sandbox-canary weight to 40% this morning for the perf test. that probably explains it.
leah: can we throttle the canary ASAP and spill traffic to euw1? we don't want cross-region fallback by default but short-term is ok.
aj: we can flip routing weight quickly: ```redwood route update --pool hosted-usw2 --route sandbox-canary --weight 10``` will cut the pressure.
infra-bot: routing change requested by aj. applying delta to edge-config. expected propagation ~20s.
alex: applying now, watching headroom and qdepth.
ops-bot: routing delta applied. new sandbox-canary weight=10.
jordan: qdepth dropping slightly, kv_evictions still high (200+/s). looks like KV cache churn from many small sequences.
sam: note: if we spill to euw1 we'll incur egress/cross-region cost — recommend short window and re-route only control-plane traffic if possible.
tanya: autoscaler didn't kick in — cooldown prevented scale (last scale-out 4m ago, pool cooldown 300s). we hit cooldown window.
leah: can we reduce cooldown for hosted-usw2 for now? it's a high-traffic hosted pool.
aj: opened quick PR to reduce cooldown to 120s: https://github.com/redwood/infra/pull/7892 (small change in autoscaler config).
alex: also let's add an alert for kv_cache_evictions > 200/s to avoid silent degradation.
ops-bot: alert rule created: gpu-kv-evictions-high (ID: 4321). will create incident if admission headroom < 5% for >10m.
alex: :thumbsup: assigning oncall to jordan for incident lead. jordan, please collect logs and start a short incident note.
jordan: On it. pulling request logs and tracing slow victims. will post a short postmortem with timeline and recommended thresholds (including reserved capacity guidance).
leah: action items: 1) temporary route weight rollback (done) 2) PR for cooldown change (aj) 3) new kv_eviction alert (ops-bot) 4) postmortem + cost/reserved-cap recs (jordan).
alex: thanks all. once traffic stabilizes let's schedule a quick retro to decide if this pool needs higher baseline reserved capacity or different cache settings.
_notes: No title field (Slack threads shouldn't have titles). Single continuous thread string. Kept messages short and Slack-like, included bot lines, links, and a small code snippet for routing change.
